packageRules.description: eclipse-temurin (Java/Kotlin's shared base image) needs a deliberate look before bumping, not an automatic merge -- confirmed for real that a JDK-25 build JVM breaks a real `gradlew build` under Gradle 8.10 + a still-common Kotlin Gradle plugin version, even though `gradle --version` alone succeeds on it (see crates/paws-java/src/lib.rs's BASE_IMAGE doc comment).

customManagers.description: crates/paws-java and crates/paws-kotlin intentionally pin the exact same eclipse-temurin tag in two places (documented as a deliberate shared pin, not an oversight) -- Renovate's built-in docker manager only scans Dockerfiles/compose files, not Rust string literals, so without this customManager these embedded image references are invisible to it.

paws-python's astral/uv base image tag encodes the pinned Python minor version (crates/paws-python/src/lib.rs's DEFAULT_PYTHON_VERSION doc comment: CPython has no self-updating "latest"/LTS tag the way node:lts-trixie does, so this is a real pin needing a real bump when a new Python minor ships). Matched against pipeline_uses_the_default_python_image's assertion specifically (anchored by function name, not just the tag shape) -- the production constant only holds the bare "3.13" fragment `format!` interpolates into it, and a second test (pipeline_respects_an_explicit_python_version) asserts an unrelated, deliberately-non-default "3.11" literal in the exact same shape that must NOT be tracked as a dependency to bump.

paws-provision's install_go installer pins a real Go release (crates/paws-provision/src/lib.rs's DEFAULT_GO_VERSION doc comment: golang.org/dl's per-version install mechanism has no floating "latest" alias the way rustup's "stable"/corepack's "pnpm@latest" do).
